correctness.rationale: For one ball, joint avoidance of F before refresh and G after refresh is the mixture of one draw avoiding F∪G and two independent draws avoiding F and G. For the ordered s+t+u boxes in the factorial moment, inclusion-exclusion changes the sizes to s+t+j and s+u+i with intersection s+i+j, giving the displayed Q exactly. At fixed indices m log Q = −(s+t+u+ε(s+i+j))(log n+c+o(1))+o(1); the error is uniform in ε∈[0,1] by m/n²→0. For τ=∞ the terms with positive shared constraint count vanish, and the terms with zero count converge unchanged. For τ=0 the alternating sums vanish when an exclusive count has positive order. At all τ the resulting mixed factorial moments factor with the three claimed rates. Higher-order moments bound tails and ensure convergence of moments along any tight subsequence; the product Poisson law is moment-determinate. Finite-set truncation on the countable space gives TV, and the marginal cover probability has positive limit, so the conditional cover ratio is valid. Equal and unequal boxes give b and d in the covariance respectively, with d/a²=1+O(m/n²) in the asymptotic regime; the two distinct-box terms cancel in the limit. For zero draws the avoidance factors raised to power zero mean one, including a zero one-ball avoidance probability.

value.rationale: The complete-coverage indicator has a nondegenerate threshold law. The three limiting counts distinguish persistence of existing vacancies from creation and removal of vacancies, which the one-sample limit and a scalar correlation cannot do. The explicit retention curve answers a natural reliability question over the full refresh scale from identical samples to asymptotic independence. The result is concrete and modest; it does not claim a quantitative process approximation or unequal-coupon extension.
